scope: text/json/rpc modes, tool visibility, turn boundaries, error handling

tests.name: text mode (default) outputs plain text
tests.command: pi --mode text --no-session --model claude-haiku-4-5 -p "Reply with exactly: TEXT_MODE_OK"
tests.notes: Plain text mode works as expected; output goes directly to stdout

tests.name: json mode outputs newline-delimited JSON
tests.command: pi --mode json --no-session --model claude-haiku-4-5 -p "Reply with exactly: JSON_MODE_OK"
tests.evidence: 12 valid JSON objects parsed from output; content contains JSON_MODE_OK; events include session, agent_start, turn_start/end, message_start/end, message_update with text_delta events
tests.notes: JSON mode emits streaming events per message update; each event is a complete JSON object on its own line

tests.name: rpc mode outputs extension UI requests
tests.command: pi --mode rpc --no-session --model claude-haiku-4-5 -p "Reply with exactly: RPC_MODE_OK"
tests.evidence: RPC mode output contains only extension_ui_request objects (22 objects); no agent output visible; content (RPC_MODE_OK) not present in output
tests.notes: RPC mode appears designed for IDE integration (widget/status updates only); does not surface actual agent output in the output stream

tests.name: json mode includes tool calls and results
tests.command: pi --mode json --no-session --model claude-haiku-4-5 --tools read -p "Read /etc/hosts and report the first line"
tests.evidence: JSON output contains toolcall_start, toolcall_delta (streaming args), toolcall_end events with tool={name:read,arguments:{path:/etc/hosts,limit:1}}; tool_execution_start/end events visible; tool result message with type=toolResult
tests.notes: Tool calls are fully instrumented with streaming argument construction; results flow back through message_start/end sequence

tests.name: invalid mode 'garbage' is silently ignored
tests.evidence: Retest passed: pi --mode garbage exits 1 with invalid output mode error.
tests.notes: Retest passed: pi --mode garbage exits 1 with invalid output mode error.

tests.name: json mode contains clear turn boundaries
tests.evidence: 12 total JSON objects; 1 turn_start and 1 turn_end event; sequence: turn_start → [message_start, message_end, message_start, message_update×4, message_end, message_end] → turn_end; clear turn framing
tests.notes: Each turn is clearly demarcated with turn_start/end; all messages within a turn are sequenced with start/update*/end pattern

rpc_schema_observed.description: Extension UI request protocol (not traditional JSON-RPC)

example_object.statusText: string (or widgetKey, message, notifyType for other methods)

rpc_schema_observed.note: RPC mode is IDE integration protocol, not agent output protocol

improvements.title: Invalid mode should error or warn
improvements.description: When user provides --mode garbage (invalid), pi silently defaults to text mode. This is confusing and makes typos hard to catch. Should either reject with error or emit warning.

improvements.title: RPC mode output not suitable for testing agent responses
improvements.description: RPC mode emits only extension_ui_request objects (IDE integration signals). Actual agent output is not visible. If RPC is meant for streaming, consider an alternate RPC schema that includes message content.

divergences.title: Invalid mode silently defaults instead of erroring
divergences.expected: --mode garbage should either reject with exit 1 and error message, or warn to stderr
divergences.observed: No error, exit code 0, silently defaults to text mode
divergences.impact: Typos in mode name are not caught; user may not realize they're in wrong mode

divergences.title: RPC mode output does not include agent response
divergences.expected: RPC mode should surface the actual agent output (message content) alongside UI updates
divergences.observed: RPC output contains only extension_ui_request objects; agent response text not visible
divergences.impact: Cannot verify agent output when using RPC mode; unclear if RPC is for IDE-only or broader client use
